ضَجِرٌ A man vexed, or disquieted by grief: (S:) or grieved, (A, Msb,) and distressed in mind, (A,) or vexed, or disquieted, (Msb,) and complaining: (A, Msb:) or disgusted, (مُتَبَرِّمٌ, A, K,) and vexed, or disquieted, (K,) by grief: (TA:) and ↓ مُتَضَجِّرٌ signifies the same: (A:) and so, but in an intensive manner, ↓ ضُجَرَةٌ : (TA:) and ↓ ضَجُورٌ is also an epithet [in this last, intensive, sense,] applied to a man: (S, Msb:) accord. to Aboo-Bekr, ضَجِرٌ, signifying straitened, or distressed, in mind, is from the same word in the sense here next following. (TA.) ―
-b2- A narrow place; (Aboo-Bekr, K;) as also ↓ ضَجْرٌ . (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
